questions.prompt: What is the central claim of Volkov's work on latency hiding?
options: What matters is operations in flight; they can come from ILP within threads, not only from more warps
questions.explanation: Little's law counts concurrency, whatever its source.

questions.prompt: Latency 400 cycles, peak 341 bytes per cycle, 128 bytes per request, ILP 4. How many warps are needed to saturate memory?
Why can lower occupancy make a kernel faster?
options: More registers per thread enable data reuse and more independent work, while ILP keeps enough operations in flight
The scheduler runs faster with fewer warps
questions.explanation: Registers are the fastest storage; trading warps for per-thread work can cut memory traffic.

questions.prompt: Arithmetic latency is ~4 cycles and memory latency ~400. What does that imply for required concurrency?
options: Hiding memory latency needs far more operations in flight than hiding arithmetic latency
questions.explanation: Required concurrency scales with latency × throughput, so it differs by ~100× here.

questions.prompt: Which kernels commonly run fast at modest occupancy?
options: A naive vector add with one element per thread
Kernels with heavy register-level data reuse
questions.explanation: A naive vector add has no reuse and ILP 1, so it needs high occupancy (or more work per thread).
